clue.text: Carefully select worker having ground-breaking equipment

parts.note: a hand is a manual labourer, as in a farm hand
a pick is the tool used to break up hard ground

explanation.surface: A labourer chosen carefully because he brings his own digging tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground-breaking' looks like praise for innovation but is meant literally: a pick breaks the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose something by hand, one at a time, is to select it with care.

clue.text: European cracks problem using computers etc

indicators.note: the European breaks into the problem, splitting it open as a crack does

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: A European solves a computing problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced technology, the computerised and electronic kind, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Leather from sheepskin apparently

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words sheepskin apparently, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: A leather seems to come from sheepskin.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'sheepskin' into the start of 'apparently'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a soft leather, traditionally made from sheep or lamb skin.

clue.text: Expert about to get involved in aircraft design

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

indicators.note: the abbreviation for about is put inside the aircraft word

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A specialist joins the team designing an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to plan or devise a scheme is to design it; a scheme is also a design.

clue.text: Worry business people are holding back

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: the word for people encloses the word for back

parts.note: a nation is a people
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A firm's staff are anxious and hanging back.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismayed alarm or anxiety is a strong form of worry.

clue.text: After retiring in office, yours truly worked for a short time

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the assembled letters are read in reverse
the word for yours truly sits inside the office word

parts.note: DEPT is short for department, an office
the setter referring to himself is ME

explanation.surface: Someone back at the office after retiring, doing short-term work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests leaving work, but it signals reading ME-in-DEPT backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A temp is a temporary worker, so this past-tense verb means did short-term work.

clue.text: Sculptor's record, using stone from Germany

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
Stein is the German word for stone

explanation.surface: A sculptor's work, made with German stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Sculptor is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Epstein was a famous twentieth-century sculptor.

clue.text: Nixon, say, concealed papers in here

indicators.note: the papers are hidden away inside the word for here
places the papers within the word for here

parts.note: present means here, in attendance
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Nixon hid incriminating papers somewhere in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Nixon was an example of a US head of state.

clue.text: Go off school in time

indicators.note: the school name sits inside the time word

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: School gets out on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb that explodes is said to go off.

clue.text: After tea, new storm

indicators.note: the letter for new comes after the tea brand

parts.note: Typhoo is a British brand of tea

explanation.surface: After a cup of tea, a fresh storm breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: TYPHOO is a well-known British brand of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical cyclone in the western Pacific is a violent storm.

clue.text: Sons will tuck into venison and finish off suet pudding

indicators.note: the two sons go inside the venison word, as eaters tuck into food

parts.note: venison is deer meat
S is son, so two sons give SS

indicators.note: takes the final letter of suet

explanation.surface: Boys eating venison then finishing a suet pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'pudding' is a general word for the sweet course.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudding is the everyday British word for the sweet course of a meal.

clue.text: Screen award I've flourished in front of admirer

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come before the admirer word
words waved about with a flourish are rearranged

parts.note: a lover is an admirer

explanation.surface: Someone brandishes an award before a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen something is to hide or conceal it, which the idiom expresses.

clue.text: Be desperate for cocaine before party

indicators.note: the cocaine letter comes ahead of the party word

parts.note: C is slang for cocaine
a rave is a dance party

explanation.surface: Someone desperate for drugs before a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something intensely is to be desperate for it.

clue.text: Actor, right old one, appearing in function briefly

indicators.note: the right, old and one pieces appear inside the short function
the function is written in its short form, as on a calculator key, so its tail is cut

parts.note: tangent is a trigonometric function
R is right
aged means old
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An elderly actor turns up at a short function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a social event but is a maths function, tangent, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who plays serious roles in plays of disaster and death is an actor.

clue.text: Surprisingly Internet meant fun

indicators.note: the letters arrive in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Unexpectedly, the web proved enjoyable.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement or diversion is fun.

clue.text: Vehicle, say, used in competition, reversing

indicators.note: the say word is placed inside the turned competition word
the competition word is read backwards

parts.note: a race is a competition
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A car in a race, going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is not 'for example' but a verb meaning state; the RACE goes backwards around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long car with rear loading space, called a station wagon in the US, is a vehicle.

clue.text: Caught nasty crone looking angry?

indicators.note: a nasty mix-up rearranges the letters

parts.note: someone angry goes red in the face

explanation.surface: A spiteful old woman flushed with anger after being trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapped with no way out means caught.

clue.text: Where clock's numbers can be seen, apparently

definitions.text: Where clock's numbers can be seen
definitions.meaning: the hour numerals are on the clock face, literally

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means judging by outward appearance; literally a clock's numerals lie on its dial.

clue.text: Search river in which former dictator drowned

indicators.note: the dictator is submerged within the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

explanation.surface: Search the river where a deposed tyrant drowned.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something closely, to scrutinise, is to search it.

clue.text: Transport some soldiers in battle

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed inside the battle word

parts.note: a fight is a battle
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Moving troops into combat.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to carry goods by transport, especially in bulk.

clue.text: Priceless musical instrument, note, held up

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a sitar is an Indian stringed instrument
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A priceless instrument raised aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Priceless' suggests invaluable, but here it means costing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something free of charge has no price at all.

clue.text: Fellow in lane that endlessly winds

indicators.note: a winding lane twists its letters
the last letter of that is dropped

explanation.surface: A man in a winding country lane.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name stands for a fellow, as names often do in crosswords.

clue.text: Number three? Wrong

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Is number three incorrect?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure, but is read as numb-er: something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: This volatile liquid was an early anaesthetic, something that deadens feeling.

clue.text: Former PM escaping row in air terminal

indicators.note: the row slips away from the airport name

parts.note: Heathrow is London's main airport

explanation.surface: An ex-prime minister fleeing a quarrel at the airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Heath was UK prime minister 1970 to 1974.

clue.text: Loud disturbance right at start of sale, after article's disposed of

indicators.note: the right letter goes at the front

parts.note: R is right

indicators.note: the article is removed from the sale word

parts.note: an auction is a sale
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A noisy row at the opening of a sale once an item is sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like an item for sale but is grammatical: the word A.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy quarrel or uproar is a loud disturbance.

clue.text: Swamped by tax, old lady becomes homeless

indicators.note: the old lady is engulfed by the tax

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
gran is grandmother

explanation.surface: A grandmother overwhelmed by taxes loses her home.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no settled home is homeless.

clue.text: Education newspaper staff rejected in part of southern England

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the TES is the Times Educational Supplement
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: An education paper's staff are turned away in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but is a stick. Dorset is a county on the English south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A county on England's south coast is part of southern England.

clue.text: Villains turning the screw

indicators.note: a turning screw twists its letters round

explanation.surface: Bad guys tightening the screw.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes The Turn of the Screw.
explanation.definitionFit: Despicable people, scoundrels, are villains.
